sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: At their peak in the mid-90s, there were about two and a half million payphones in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在90年代中期的高峰期，美国大约有二百五十万个公用电话。

sentences.en: The adoption of cell phones has brought that number down further and further every year.
sentences.zh: 手机的普及让这个数字每年都在不断下降。

sentences.en: The fully enclosed outdoor telephone box, you know the one that Superman changes in?
sentences.zh: 全封闭的户外电话亭，你知道超人换衣服的那种吗？

sentences.en: That is exceptionally rare.
sentences.zh: 那个极其罕见。

sentences.en: Only four of those are left in New York City.
sentences.zh: 纽约市现在只剩下四个了。

sentences.en: After several decades, these little pieces of single-use architecture just disappeared from the landscape.
sentences.zh: 几十年后，这些一次性建筑的小物件就从地表上消失了。

sentences.en: They simply weren't popular enough to justify their existence.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不够受欢迎，无法维持自身的存在。

sentences.en: But there's always an exception to the rule.
sentences.zh: 但这条规则总有例外。

sentences.en: Twenty years ago, a man discovered a phone booth in the middle of the desert that became his obsession.
sentences.zh: 二十年前，一个男人在沙漠中央发现了一个电话亭，并为此着迷。

sentences.en: An obsession that he then passed on to the world at large.
sentences.zh: 这种迷恋后来被他传递给了全世界。

sentences.en: From the great radio program Snap Judgment of Oakland, California,
sentences.zh: 来自加利福尼亚州奥克兰伟大的广播节目《瞬息决断》，

sentences.en: producer Joe Rosenberg tells the story of a very special phone booth in the middle of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 制作人乔·罗森伯格讲述了一个位于荒凉之地的特别电话亭的故事。

sentences.en: Okay, so this story starts out back in the mid-90s in Phoenix, where Godfrey Daniels...
sentences.zh: 好的，这个故事要从90年代中期凤凰城讲起，当时戈弗雷·丹尼尔斯……

sentences.en: My given name is Godfrey Daniels, but I go by Doc.
sentences.zh: 我的本名是戈弗雷·丹尼尔斯，但大家都叫我多克。

sentences.en: He's heading back home after seeing this band, Girl Trouble.
sentences.zh: 他在看完一个叫“女孩麻烦”的乐队演出后正往家赶。

sentences.en: And after the concert, someone hands him a copy of their zine.
sentences.zh: 演出结束后，有人递给他一本他们的同人杂志。

sentences.en: Remember zines?
sentences.zh: 还记得同人杂志吗？

sentences.en: If not, don't worry.
sentences.zh: 如果不记得，也没关系。

sentences.en: They're kind of like a pre-internet miniature magazine.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像互联网出现前的微型杂志。

sentences.en: So as I was walking home, I was kind of flipping through it, and on about the third or fourth page,
sentences.zh: 所以当我走在回家的路上时，我一边翻看着它，大约在第三页或第四页，

sentences.en: there were a couple of letters to the editor, and one of them mentioned that there was a phone booth
sentences.zh: 有几封读者来信，其中一封提到有一个电话亭

sentences.en: in the Mojave Desert, miles and miles from any pavement, just sitting by itself.
sentences.zh: 在莫哈韦沙漠里，方圆几英里没有任何铺装道路，就那么孤零零地立着。

sentences.en: And this, for Doc, just made no sense.
sentences.zh: 而对多克来说，这完全说不通。

sentences.en: I wasn't sure that I believed it.
sentences.zh: 我不确定自己是否相信。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Well, I didn't have any reason to believe it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没有任何理由相信它。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know if, in the age of cell phones, if it's the same,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不知道在手机时代是不是还一样，

sentences.en: but when you were out in the desert in those days, you were on your own.
sentences.zh: 但在当年的沙漠里，你只能靠自己。

sentences.en: You couldn't call people.
sentences.zh: 你没法给别人打电话。

sentences.en: So the idea that there could be this phone booth just sitting out in an uncontactable place,
sentences.zh: 所以这样一个电话亭竟然坐落在无法联系上的地方，

sentences.en: it was kind of like if somebody was on the moon, you know, and you could talk to somebody on the moon.
sentences.zh: 这就好比有人在月球上，你知道的，你可以和月球上的人通话。

sentences.en: Where did he say it was exactly?
sentences.zh: 他具体说在哪儿了吗？

sentences.en: Like, what was the nearest recognizable landmark?
sentences.zh: 比如，最近的可辨认地标是什么？

sentences.en: He didn't say it.
sentences.zh: 他没说。

sentences.en: It was a really short little paragraph.
sentences.zh: 那只是一小段非常短的文字。

sentences.en: There wasn't any solid information, really, other than the number.
sentences.zh: 除了电话号码，真的没有什么切实的信源。

sentences.en: And so when Doc got home, he thought, okay, why not give it a shot?
sentences.zh: 所以当多克回到家时，他想，好吧，为什么不试试呢？

sentences.en: And I jabbed in the number, and it just rang.
sentences.zh: 然后我拨了那个号码，它就通了。

sentences.en: And I let it ring for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我让它响了很久。

sentences.en: And I was just imagining making a phone ring out where, presumably,
sentences.zh: 我只是在想象着让一个电话在那种地方响起来，据推测，

sentences.en: no one could hear it except the coyotes.
sentences.zh: 除了郊狼，没人能听到。

sentences.en: But then there was also, in the back of your mind, the thought, what if?
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你脑海深处也会闪过一个念头：万一呢？

sentences.en: Like, what if somebody's wandering by?
sentences.zh: 比如，万一有人刚好路过呢？

sentences.en: Who would be out there?
sentences.zh: 谁会去那种地方？

sentences.en: Who would pick up?
sentences.zh: 谁会接电话？

sentences.en: It just really grabbed me.
sentences.zh: 这真的深深吸引了我。

sentences.en: And so I hung up, and then I just kept thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我挂断了电话，然后就一直在想这件事。

sentences.en: I kept thinking about it all night long.
sentences.zh: 我整晚都在想这件事。

sentences.en: I was thinking about it as I fell asleep, and it just somehow got me into its clutches.
sentences.zh: 我快睡着时还在想，它不知怎么的就把我迷住了。

sentences.en: And so the next morning?
sentences.zh: 那么第二天早上呢？

sentences.en: I called again.
sentences.zh: 我又打了过去。

sentences.en: Then I just kind of became obsessed.
sentences.zh: 然后我就有点着魔了。

sentences.en: Soon, Doc found himself calling the phone news all the time.
sentences.zh: 很快，多克发现自己一直在给那个电话拨号。

sentences.en: When friends visited his house, he'd twist their arm and make them call it.
sentences.zh: 当朋友来他家做客时，他会软磨硬泡逼他们也打。

sentences.en: He even put up a Post-it note in the bathroom mirror.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在浴室镜子上贴了一张便签。

sentences.en: It just said, did you remember to call the Mojave Desert today?
sentences.zh: 上面写着：今天你记得给莫哈韦沙漠打电话了吗？

sentences.en: But it turned out I didn't need it because I used to call many times a day.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明我根本不需要便签，因为我以前一天要打好多次。

sentences.en: Like how many times?
sentences.zh: 大概打多少次？

sentences.en: If I was supposed to be working, I was probably calling at least once an hour.
sentences.zh: 如果我本来该工作的话，我大概每小时至少打一次。

sentences.en: And again, this is all assuming that it actually existed, which I had no proof of.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这一切都建立在它确实存在的前提下，而我对此毫无证据。

sentences.en: Like on speakerphone?
sentences.zh: 是开免提吗？

sentences.en: Or like you would stop everything?
sentences.zh: 还是说你会放下手头的一切？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, because that would require explanations.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，因为那样还得跟别人解释。

sentences.en: I would just, you know, have the phone kind of cradle against my ear.
sentences.zh: 我只会，你知道的，把电话轻轻夹在耳边。

sentences.en: You know, just listening to it ring.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就只是听着它响。

sentences.en: Doc knew it was weird to keep calling a number with no one on the other end.
sentences.zh: 多克知道，一直给一个无人接听的号码打电话很奇怪。

sentences.en: But if he was ever pressed about it, he'd say it was like being a ham radio operator.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人追问此事，他会说这就好比当个业余无线电爱好者。

sentences.en: One little person, sending the signal as far as he could into the ether.
sentences.zh: 一个小人物，尽可能地把信号发射到虚空中。

sentences.en: Wondering if another little person was out there, listening in, waiting to be contacted, in that uncontactable place.
sentences.zh: 琢磨着是否另一个小人物也在那里，正侧耳倾听，等待着被联系，就在那个无法联系的偏远角落。

sentences.en: So I figured I would be doing this forever.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时觉得我会永远这样打下去。

sentences.en: I really didn't think anybody would ever pick up the phone.
sentences.zh: 我真的从没想过会有人接电话。

sentences.en: But then, just one month after he started calling?
sentences.zh: 但就在他开始打电话的一个月后？

sentences.en: Just doing my daily call, and I got a busy signal.
sentences.zh: 我正照常打着日常的电话，结果听到了忙音。

sentences.en: So Doc actually managed to record that call.
sentences.zh: 所以多克其实设法录下了那个电话。

sentences.en: I look like I'm an idiot, because I keep saying, wow.
sentences.zh: 我看起来像个傻子，因为我一直在说，哇哦。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, I must have misdialed.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，我肯定是拨错号了。

sentences.en: So I dialed it again.
sentences.zh: 所以我又拨了一遍。

sentences.en: And it was a busy signal again.
sentences.zh: 结果还是忙音。

sentences.en: I realized, okay, either something's gone wrong with the phone company here,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，好吧，要么是电话公司出了故障，

sentences.en: or somebody is using the Mojave phone booth right now.
sentences.zh: 要么就是此刻正有人在用莫哈韦沙漠的那个电话亭。

sentences.en: I was totally hyperactive.
sentences.zh: 我当时整个人兴奋得不行。

sentences.en: My main thing was I didn't want them to get away.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里唯一的想法就是别让他们跑了。

sentences.en: Like, I was thinking, I need to catch it right when they hang up that phone.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，我必须在他们挂断电话的那一刻接通。

sentences.en: So I just redial, redial.
sentences.zh: 所以我拼命重拨，重拨。

sentences.en: And then it rang.
sentences.zh: 然后电话响了。

sentences.en: And it rang.
sentences.zh: 它响了。

sentences.en: It rang.
sentences.zh: 它一直响。

sentences.en: Four or five times.
sentences.zh: 响了四五声。

sentences.en: And I thought, oh, crap.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，糟了。

sentences.en: And then I heard a voice say, hello.
sentences.zh: 然后我听到一个声音说：喂。

sentences.en: Sadly, Doc was only able to properly record his own words at this now historic moment.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，在这个注定载入史册的时刻，多克只成功完整录下了他自己的声音。

sentences.en: But as many times as I had called, I had given remarkably little thought, if any, to what
sentences.zh: 但尽管我打过无数次电话，我却极少认真考虑过

sentences.en: I would say, you know.
sentences.zh: 我要说些什么，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I said, hello, Mojave Desert?
sentences.zh: 然后我说：喂，莫哈韦沙漠吗？

sentences.en: She said, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她说：对啊。

sentences.en: And I said, you are.
sentences.zh: 我说：真的是你啊。

sentences.en: Okay, this is going to sound like a strange question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这听起来可能是一个奇怪的问题。

sentences.en: Why are you in the middle of the Mojave Desert?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会在莫哈韦沙漠的正中央？

sentences.en: She said, I'm making my calls.
sentences.zh: 她说：我来这儿打我的电话。

sentences.en: I got to say, when I looked at the transcript, it was kind of funny because, like, you think
sentences.zh: 我得说，当我看到文字记录时觉得挺逗的，因为你会觉得，

sentences.en: everything's cool if you're like, and she's like, cinder mining.
sentences.zh: 如果她说，哦一切都挺好，然后她说：采煤渣。

sentences.en: And she's like, cinder blocks.
sentences.zh: 她说：煤渣砖。

sentences.en: And you're like, that's so cool.
sentences.zh: 而你的反应是：太酷了吧。

sentences.en: And she said that she'd never heard the phone ring before.
sentences.zh: 她说她以前从来没听见过这个电话响。

sentences.en: Can you tell me her name?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我她的名字吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, her name's Lorene.
sentences.zh: 可以，她叫洛琳。

sentences.en: And was there any sense of disappointment?
sentences.zh: 当时有任何失望的情绪吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Disappointment about what?
sentences.zh: 对什么失望？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: Well, let me put it this way.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我这么跟你说吧。

sentences.en: It's almost kind of like the idea that this phone is ringing out there in the desert and
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是一种幻想，觉得这个电话在沙漠深处孤零零地响着，

sentences.en: anyone could pick up.
sentences.zh: 任何人都有可能接听。

sentences.en: But then finally someone picks up and it's just Lorene.
sentences.zh: 但最终接听的人却只是洛琳。

sentences.en: Oh, no, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不。

sentences.en: See, I look at it the exact opposite way.
sentences.zh: 你看，我的看法恰好相反。

sentences.en: Somebody did pick up.
sentences.zh: 确实有人接了电话。

sentences.en: And I had no right to expect anyone ever would.
sentences.zh: 而我原本根本没有权利奢望任何人会接。

sentences.en: So this was great to hear a human voice in place of the ringing.
sentences.zh: 所以能听到一个真正的人声代替了单调的铃声，这感觉太棒了。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, this was a payoff.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思，这就是回报。

sentences.en: It just encouraged me more.
sentences.zh: 这更加激励了我。

sentences.en: And the instant I hung up, I kicked myself because I had forgotten to ask her what was
sentences.zh: 我挂断电话的瞬间，气得直拍大腿，因为我忘记问她

sentences.en: probably the most important question, which is where was the phone booth?
sentences.zh: 可能是最重要的问题了，那就是电话亭到底在哪儿？

sentences.en: But of course, I had no way to get in touch with her except to find the thing.
sentences.zh: 但当然，除了把那东西找出来，我没有任何办法能联系到她。

sentences.en: So Doc calls around, does some sleuthing, and a few months later gets his hands on the
sentences.zh: 于是多克四处打听，做了一番侦探工作，几个月后，他弄到了一张

sentences.en: equivalent of an X marks the spot map showing the supposed location of the Mojave phone booth.
sentences.zh: 堪称藏宝图的地图，上面标出了莫哈韦沙漠电话亭的疑似位置。

sentences.en: So I thought, oh, we're all set.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，太好了，我们万事俱备了。

sentences.en: So my friend and I took off and traveled all the day to the Mojave Desert.
sentences.zh: 于是我和朋友出发了，花了一整天时间赶往莫哈韦沙漠。

sentences.en: And this is in the middle of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 当时正值八月中旬。

sentences.en: And so it's scorching hot, just scorching hot.
sentences.zh: 所以天气热得要命，简直酷热难耐。

sentences.en: Basically, as far as you could see, you saw Joshua trees.
sentences.zh: 基本上，放眼望去，全都是约书亚树。

sentences.en: And then we saw this little dirt path that was marked, you know, danger, danger, warning,
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到了一条标有路标的小泥路，上面写着：危险，危险，警告，

sentences.en: not maintained, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 无人维护，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: And that was the road we were supposed to take.
sentences.zh: 而那条就是我们本该走的路。

sentences.en: So we were, you know, we were just going along and going along.
sentences.zh: 所以我们，你知道的，就一直在路上开啊开。

sentences.en: And at first I thought, oh, this is not bad at all.
sentences.zh: 起初我还想，哦，这路况其实也还行嘛。

sentences.en: But the further along that we went, the road would narrow.
sentences.zh: 但我们开得越远，路就越窄。

sentences.en: And the thing was that the sun was going down.
sentences.zh: 关键是太阳正在下山。

sentences.en: And in the daytime, you've got these grand, huge vistas.
sentences.zh: 在白天，你视野开阔，景色壮观。

sentences.en: And you kind of have a sense of where you are.
sentences.zh: 你大致知道自己身处何方。

sentences.en: But when the darkness drops, it's just whatever you can see right in front of you.
sentences.zh: 但当夜幕降临，你所能看到的就只有车灯直射眼前的那么一小块地方了。

sentences.en: And we were ringed by storMs.
sentences.zh: 而且我们被暴风雨包围了。

sentences.en: There was lightning almost in every direction.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个方向都有闪电。

sentences.en: So then I started to think, if we have any kind of a problem,
sentences.zh: 于是我开始琢磨，如果我们遇到任何麻烦，

sentences.en: unless we do find the phone booth, we have no way of, you know,
sentences.zh: 除非我们能找到那个电话亭，否则我们根本没有办法，你知道的，

sentences.en: letting people know we're really in trouble.
sentences.zh: 让别人知道我们真的陷入困境了。

sentences.en: But at a certain point, just barely in the reach of the headlights,
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，就在车灯照射范围的边缘处，

sentences.en: I thought I saw a line of telephone poles.
sentences.zh: 我以为我看到了一排电话线杆。

sentences.en: And there was a little jut to the left and then a little jut to the right.
sentences.zh: 然后稍微向左拐了一点，接着又向右拐了一点。

sentences.en: And I brought the van to a stop with the headlights just shining right on the Mojave phone booth.
sentences.zh: 我把面包车停了下来，车头灯正好照着莫哈韦沙漠的那个电话亭。

sentences.en: And it was really, it was really quite a moment.
sentences.zh: 那感觉真是，真是相当奇妙的一刻。

sentences.en: And there's bullet holes in it.
sentences.zh: 上面有弹孔。

sentences.en: There's no glass.
sentences.zh: 玻璃都没了。

sentences.en: It's all busted out.
sentences.zh: 全碎光了。

sentences.en: It's kind of a wreck, you know.
sentences.zh: 有点像个废墟，你知道的。

sentences.en: But to me, it was just, it was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，它就是，它太美了。

sentences.en: I needed to hear that phone ring.
sentences.zh: 我需要听到那个电话铃响。

sentences.en: I needed to hear what I had been causing to happen all this time out there.
sentences.zh: 我需要听到我这段时间一直在那里引发这一切的声音。

sentences.en: So I called, I called my friend's pager.
sentences.zh: 所以我打了，我打了朋友的寻呼机。

sentences.en: And here I am, out in the Mojave, surrounded by Joshua trees and lightning and desert.
sentences.zh: 而现在我身处莫哈韦沙漠，四周环绕着约书亚树、闪电和荒漠。

sentences.en: And now there's a familiar...
sentences.zh: 现在有一个熟悉的……

sentences.en: It was just, and it was so loud.
sentences.zh: 简直是，声音太大了。

sentences.en: It was really loud.
sentences.zh: 声音真的很大。

sentences.en: The bell was just crazy loud.
sentences.zh: 铃声简直大得离谱。

sentences.en: For me, that was kind of the moment, is hearing that phone ring.
